pending_commit.commit_message: bluetooth: Export GATT attribute interfaces as GATT client role In order to make the GATT attributes visible to D-Bus clients, this includes the following changes. - Adding gatt_interface_handler to export the discovered GATT services characteristics and descriptor to D-Bus - Implementation of observer mechanism in gatt.cc so that gatt_interface_handler can get notified on changes on GATT attributes - Determining how the D-Bus object properties should be updated and exported. UPSTREAM: Bluetooth: btrtl: add support for retrieving the UART settings The UART settings are embedded in the config blob. This has to be parsed to successfully initialize the Bluetooth part of the RTL8723BS (which is an SDIO chip, but the Bluetooth part is connected via UART). The Realtek "rtl8723bs_bt" and "rtl8723ds_bt" userspace Bluetooth UART initialization tools (rtk_hciattach) use the following sequence: - send H5 sync pattern (already supported by hci_h5) - get LMP version (already supported by btrtl) - get ROM version (already supported by btrtl) - load the firmware and config for the current chipset (already supported by btrtl) - read UART settings from the config blob (part of this patch) - send UART settings via a vendor command to the device (which changes the baudrate of the device and enables or disables flow control depending on the config) - change the baudrate and flow control settings on the host - send the firmware and config blob to the device (already supported by btrtl) Sending the last firmware and config blob download command (rtl_download_cmd) fails if the UART settings are not updated beforehand. This is presumably because the device applies the config right after the firmware and config blob download - which means that at this point the host is using different UART settings than the device (which will obviously result in non-working communication). UPSTREAM: Bluetooth: btrtl: add support for the RTL8723BS and RTL8723DS chips The Realtek RTL8723BS and RTL8723DS chipsets are SDIO wifi chips. They also contain a Bluetooth module which is connected via UART to the host. Realtek's userspace initialization tool (rtk_hciattach) differentiates these two via the HCI version and revision returned by the HCI_OP_READ_LOCAL_VERSION command. Additionally we apply these checks only the for UART devices. Everything else is assumed to be a "RTL8723B" which was originally supported by the driver (communicating via USB). UPSTREAM: Bluetooth: btusb: Add a Kconfig option to enable USB autosuspend by default On many laptops the btusb device is the only USB device not having USB autosuspend enabled, this causes not only the HCI but also the USB controller to stay awake, together using aprox. 0.4W of power. Modern ultrabooks idle around 6W (at 50% screen brightness), 3.5W for Apollo Lake devices. 0.4W is a significant chunk of this (7 / 11%). The btusb driver already contains code to allow enabling USB autosuspend, but currently leaves it up to the user / userspace to enable it. This means that for most people it will not be enabled, leading to an unnecessarily high power consumption. Since enabling it is not entirely without risk of regressions, this commit adds a Kconfig option so that Linux distributions can choose to enable it by default. This commit also adds a module option so that when distros receive bugs they can easily ask the user to disable it again for easy debugging. biod: bio_crypto_init stall boot It is possible for bio_crypto_init to still be running when boot-update-firmware is started. This is not good because both tasks interact with the fingerprint MCU in different incompatible ways. This change makes bio_crypto_init an upstart "task". This allows bio_crypto_init to stall the boot at the boot-services step, until bio_crypto_init has fully finished. This has the effect of delaying boot-update-firmware until bio_crypto_init has finished. Additionally, this ensures that fewer system processes are running while the seed is being set. The boot time implications have been analyzed in the following speadsheet: http://sheets/1O3QYv4KNZeqm-o_0_HQc9Z7BcP-FsAN_Gs9f9mk5jyc#gid=274630119 The discussion of the boot time implications are in the following bugs: BUG=b:130677245, b:119206742, chromium:992487 TEST=emerge-nocturne biod && cros deploy dut1 biod reboot TEST=emerge-nocturne biod && cros deploy dut1 biod ssh dut1 touch /var/log/biofw # Add the following to the top of the main script # section of/etc/init/bio_crypto_init.conf sleep 30 # Add the following to the end of the post-start # section of /etc/init/bio_crypto_init.conf rm /var/log/biofw # Add the following to top of the pre-start section # of /etc/init/boot-update-firmware.conf if [ -e /var/log/biofw ]; then logger -t "${UPSTART_JOB}" "bio_crypto_init is still running" else logger -t "${UPSTART_JOB}" "bio_crypto_init is NOT still running" fi # Now clear the logs and reboot rm -rf /var/log/* reboot grep --text bio_crypto_init /var/log/messages # Check that you see "bio_crypto_init is NOT still running" TEST=# Fetch nocturne device emerge-nocturne biod && cros deploy dut1 biod gsutil cat gs://chromeos-binaries/HOME/bcs-nocturne-private/overlay-nocturne-private/chromeos-base/chromeos-firmware-fpmcu-nocturne/nocturne_fp-2.2.67.tbz2 | tar xjv -C /tmp ssh dut1 mount -oremount,rw / scp /tmp/nocturne_fp_*.bin dut1:~/ ssh dut1 'flashrom --fast-verify --programmer=ec:type=fp --image=EC_RW --write ~/nocturne_fp_*.bin' ssh dut1 cat /dev/cros_fp ssh dut1 rm -rf '/var/log/*' ssh dut1 reboot ssh dut1 cat '/var/log/bio_crypto_init/bio_crypto_init.*' '/var/log/biod/bio_fw_updater.*' # Check that there are no errors Change-Id: Ieba22bde6263f373949e1f743eb0e6f5c78ffccf Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1725576 Tested-by: Craig Hesling <hesling@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nicolas Norvez <norvez@chromium.org>

diagnostics: update cros_healthd's init script cros_healthd's ProbeNonRemovableBlockDevices method works outside of the minijail sandbox, but not inside. To fix this, we need to mount parts of /sys and /dev inside the minijail. cros_healthd attempts to discover nonremovable block devices programmatically, so it doesn't make sense to mount specific paths within /sys or /dev when these paths could vary per device or over time. Also, add the -G argument to the minijail call, so that cros_healthd enters the minijail as a member of the disk group. This is necessary to get access to the block /dev nodes.
